subject: Mythology
title: The Yoruba Creation: Olorun and Obatala
description: A fast breakdown of The Yoruba Creation: Olorun and Obatala for builders.

hook.text: In Yoruba mythology, the earth was created when a god poured sand from a snail shell onto the primordial waters.

buildup.text: Olorun, the supreme god, sent Obatala down from heaven on a golden chain carrying sand, a hen, and a palm nut.

discovery.text: Obatala poured the sand. The hen scratched it in every direction, spreading the land across the ocean.

twist.text: While shaping humans from clay, Obatala drank palm wine and made some imperfectly. He vowed to protect the disabled.

climax.text: The Yoruba creation story became the foundation of multiple religions practiced by over 100 million people today.

punchline.text: A snail shell, a hen, and sand — that is all it took to make the world.

quiz.question: Why does Obatala protect disabled people in Yoruba mythology?
options: They are considered sacred messengers of the gods
He accidentally shaped some humans imperfectly while drunk and vowed to protect them
Olorun commanded him to guard the most vulnerable
